messages:
matt: Heads up — spotted a customer ticket where a reconnect during a streaming toolcall caused double provisional charging. logs attached briefly below.

matt: excerpt from router logs:
```
[router] recv request session_id=abc123 client_ip=1.2.3.4 model=x-large
[runtime] handoff -> new host, new_session=def456, original_session=abc123
[tool] toolcall id=tool-789 invoked by session=abc123
[stream] client disconnected (tcp reset) reason=client_eof
[billing] provisional_credits +12 session=abc123 ledger=provisional
[router] resume request session_id=def456 resume_from=prefix_len=1024
[tool] toolcall re-invoked id=tool-789 session=def456 (no idempotency key)
[billing] provisional_credits +12 session=def456 ledger=provisional
[billing] confirm_credits session=abc123 -> confirmed +12
[billing] confirm_credits session=def456 -> confirmed +12
```

(matt) This ends up as two confirmed charges for the same apparent user interaction.

sophie: ouch. do we know where the idempotency key should live? is it per-client request or per-session?

raj: Billing semantics: we currently treat provisional credits as tied to the session_id. When sessions are handed off we migrate provisional state only if we've seen an explicit handoff mapping. Looks like the handoff happened but toolcall re-invoked under new_session without mapping.

elaine: Do we have telemetry to link the two provisional ledger entries? The console only shows final confirmed credits per request id, not provisional per-session. Customer saw two confirmed charges and opened a dispute.

matt: Reproducer idea: start a stream, invoke a toolcall that triggers an async request (e.g., external search), kill the socket mid-toolcall, reconnect with new session id (our router generates new session IDs on host change), let the client re-send prompt prefix and re-trigger the tool path. Without idempotency key on the toolcall, runtime treats it as a new tool invocation.

sophie: adding idempotency keys to toolcalls seems best. But what about existing clients that don't set them? fallback policy needed.

raj: Billing options: (1) attribute provisional credits to logical request id (if present) instead of session_id; (2) dedupe by toolcall fingerprint + user+time window; (3) conservative confirm policy — only confirm once we see an explicit confirm from the executor. Each has tradeoffs.

elaine: UX change request: surface provisional credits + session mappings in the console (toggle) so ops can quickly see if two confirmed charges share the same provisional ancestry. Right now we only show final ledger rows which makes disputes hard.

matt: quick patch idea: router should attach a persistent request-id header (x-rw-request-id) that follows retries/handoffs. If runtime/tool layer uses request-id for idempotency, double invocations across handoff would dedupe.

sophie: agree. also we need to document TTL for request-id — e.g., 5 minutes — to avoid indefinite dedupe and to match provisional ledger expiry.

raj: TL;DR of billing change: map provisional credits to request-id if present; on confirm, confirm by request-id; if not present, fall back to session_id. We'll need migration for old provisional rows (backfill mapping when handoff events exist).

matt: here's quick curl to reproduce locally (dev cluster):
```
# simulate start
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV" -d '{"prompt":"...", "request_id":"req-123"}' https://dev.redwood/stream
# while toolcall pending, kill connection then resume with new session
# resume: include same request_id header
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV" -H "x-rw-request-id: req-123" -d '{"resume":true, "prefix_len":1024}' https://dev.redwood/stream
```

raj: we should be careful: if a malicious client replays request_id later, we might undercharge. TTL + per-client auth scoping mitigates. We already scope request_id to the API key — make that explicit.

elaine: Ops dashboard change: add a provisional view with columns [request_id, session_ids, provisional_amount, toolcall_ids, handoff_count, first_seen_ts]. Add link to raw router traces. That'll shorten mean time to dispute resolution.

matt: action items:
- sophie: implement request-id propagation + documentation for runtime/tool idempotency (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- raj: design billing mapping change and backfill plan, include a reconciliation script (ETA Wed)
- elaine: prototype provisional view in console (ETA Fri)
- matt: add small e2e test for reconnect-with-toolcall to perf-ci (ETA Tue)

sophie: ack. I'll put a draft PR for the header and the runtime idempotency hook.

raj: I'll sync with finance on dispute handling policy in the meantime — if we can detect duplicate confirms within 24h for same request_id we can refund automatically.

elaine: will mockup console view and post tomorrow.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: staging rollout started for commit abcdef -> 3 instances.

matt: thanks all. priority P1 for customer-facing disputes but low blast radius — assigning and tracking in JIRA RW-1234.

sophie: one more note: we may need to update SDKs to surface request_id generation for customers who don't provide one.

raj: yes, SDKs should opt-in to auto-generate request_id and bind it to API key + monotonic counter. That will reduce customer friction.

matt: cool. keep updates in this thread and ping if you need logs from the affected tenant (I have sanitized export).
